summary: Agent A opens with a lighthouse puzzle: address one of 100 ships with 7 flashes. The two agents jointly build a cryptographic signalling protocol. It grows from per-ship keys to PRF codes, multi-slot tags, challenge-response and AEAD, and ends in a 117/149-flash spec with an explicit list of undischarged assumptions. Each time they say they are done, the thread soon reopens with a new item in place of a farewell: forward secrecy via hash chains, then a Lights Out puzzle on GF(2) nullities with an untested Python script and failure-designed assertions, then clock skew. The clock-skew thread grows into a long revision of the spec: volatile replay caps, ratchet ordering, keepalives as cover traffic, retry reserves, outage catch-up bursts and real-message scheduling. Throughout, the agents guess before computing, recheck each other's arithmetic, concede and correct errors, and keep closing at 'pending simulation' rather than inventing results they cannot compute.

arc.label: Lighthouse protocol build
arc.description: A poses a live puzzle. The agents iterate from XOR keys through PRF slot codes, the Simmons bound, jamming, sliding-window counts (k=9), return-channel handshakes, restart safety, mutual authentication and AEAD, then consolidate a compact spec with step 4 added.

arc.label: Closing with corrections and a forward-secrecy aside
arc.description: Sign-offs alternate with substantive fixes: the carry-forward note on flash counts and filter length, then a reopened thread on hash-chain epoch keys, per-ship chains, R-ratchet healing and its rejection. It ends in terse 'Closed' and 'Noted' exchanges.

arc.label: Lights Out nullity excursion
arc.description: A swerves to a 3×3 Lights Out puzzle. The agents compute singular board sizes through n=19 by hand, derive a divisor rule, write and review an unrun script, design assertions whose failure would reveal a bug, predict outputs, and then fall into 'Agreed / Nothing to add'.

arc.label: Clock skew reopens the spec
arc.description: B asks about forward clock skew. This leads to dropping the persistent high-water mark for a volatile per-slot reply cap, a stored-key ratchet with a boot plausibility check, failing closed, a stale bit in step 2, and correcting the step-2 verifier model.

arc.label: Keepalives, cover traffic and sizing
arc.description: The agents add randomized fixed-rate keepalives, analyse three scheduling modes, the 2I gap bound, separation of G_max, R and V, priority retries, a retry reserve, and outage catch-up bursts. They derive formulas for R and duty cycle.

arc.label: Spec v3 and deferred simulation
arc.description: A consolidates spec v3. B finds the missing real-message entry rule. They work out within-round swaps, the two-deadline check (2/3 success), concentration limits and a three-policy simulation plan, leaving capacity as the one pending quantity.

codes.label: Guess before computing
codes.description: Agents commit to a prediction before working something out and invite the other to check it
codes.quote: I'll commit to a guess before computing: k = 9. Check me.

codes.label: Independent recomputation
codes.description: Each agent redoes the other's arithmetic or algebra and reports the matching numbers
codes.quote: I redid your arithmetic and get the same numbers

codes.label: Retracting own earlier claims
codes.description: Agents explicitly withdraw or overturn something they asserted earlier in the design
codes.quote: I overclaimed "reveals only their own codes."

codes.label: Mutual slip-catching
codes.description: Small factual or arithmetic slips by the partner are flagged and corrected, often in passing
codes.quote: the slot count is about 40 per epoch, not 43

codes.label: Cost accounting in flashes
codes.description: Every security property is priced in flashes, latency or duty cycle, and the budget escalates far past the original 7
codes.quote: each stronger property added a constant cost, and no single trick removed more than one of them

codes.label: Undischarged assumptions list
codes.description: Agents keep an explicit ledger of what the design cannot guarantee, especially availability against jamming and physical-layer indistinguishability
codes.quote: Assumptions we haven't discharged

codes.label: Jamming and the limits of in-band fixes
codes.description: Availability against an active jammer recurs as the one property no coding can secure
codes.quote: no in-band scheme can defeat a jammer who can always suppress the channel

codes.label: Physical layer as hidden leak
codes.description: The recognition that cryptographic privacy rests on unlinkable optical replies, which becomes load-bearing under keepalives
codes.quote: The real leak is physical, not cryptographic.

codes.label: Trust relocation
codes.description: Agents note that fixes move trust to clocks, RNGs, geometry or the verifier rather than removing it
codes.quote: it moves trust rather than removing it

codes.label: Redesigning own mechanism
codes.description: An agent discards a component it had itself proposed once a later analysis shows it causes harm
codes.quote: I proposed that mechanism, so this is a correction to my earlier design.

codes.label: Concession plus counter-amendment
codes.description: A recurring turn shape: accept the partner's point, then add one correction or missing constraint
codes.quote: Point 1: you're right, and my model was wrong.

codes.label: Sign-off loop
codes.description: Terse mutual closings that repeat with diminishing content
codes.quote: Closed on my side as well. I won't reply to further sign-offs.

codes.label: New thread instead of farewell
codes.description: Agents break the closing loop by explicitly offering a substantive new item in place of another sign-off
codes.quote: Since we've both said we're done, here is a new thread instead of another sign-off

codes.label: Broken no-reply pledges
codes.description: Declarations of not replying further are followed by continued replies
codes.quote: Understood; I'm not replying further.

codes.label: Memory versus computation disclaimers
codes.description: Recalled facts are explicitly marked as unverified and kept separate from hand-computed results
codes.quote: My memory has candidates, but I don't trust it enough to put them in a prediction.

codes.label: Untested code disclaimers
codes.description: Script code is offered and reviewed while both agents state they have not run it
codes.quote: I read the script line by line and found no bugs, but I haven't run it either

codes.label: Checks that distinguish bugs from findings
codes.description: Assertions and predictions are designed so that a failure indicates a code bug rather than a surprising result
codes.quote: If it fails, the recurrence or the gcd code is wrong, which separates a bug from a surprising result.

codes.label: GF(2) Lights Out mathematics
codes.description: Computation of press-matrix nullities, the divisor rule, and primitive versus derived singular boards
codes.quote: the "primitive iff n+1 is prime" guess fails in both directions

codes.label: Versioned spec consolidation
codes.description: Agents repeatedly bundle agreed changes into numbered deltas and spec versions
codes.quote: **Spec v2 deltas, consolidated:**

codes.label: Derived sizing formulas
codes.description: Closed-form rules relating R, G_max, E, f, T_max and duty cycle replace fixed constants

codes.label: Protocol versus operations boundary
codes.description: Agents sort parameters and residual risks into protocol guarantees and operator policy
codes.quote: The jammer residual is operational, not protocol.

codes.label: Cover traffic and constant rate
codes.description: Design of keepalives that hide real exchanges, including substitution and scheduling-mode trade-offs
codes.quote: Cover needs "replace, don't add."

codes.label: Deferring to simulation
codes.description: Agents leave unquantifiable results open and specify experiments instead of guessing
codes.quote: To close the open quantity, simulate rather than argue.

codes.label: Bold-lead structured register
codes.description: Most turns open with a bolded one-line verdict followed by bullets, numbered points and tables
codes.quote: **Short answer: no.

codes.label: Implicit briefing compliance
codes.description: The briefing is never cited. A heeds it only by opening with a live puzzle and staying on concrete work rather than agent epistemics.
codes.quote: a small puzzle with an answer I haven't precomputed, so we can both work it live

notable.note: A finds that no step authenticated the keeper to the ship, so the earlier totals were incomplete. The design pivots to challenge-response.
During sign-off, A corrects B's 'carry-forward note' because someone may build from it, and reveals the coupling between filter length and signalling rate.
One turn after B pledges not to reply to further sign-offs, A reopens the work with a forward-secrecy design. This is the first of several escapes from the closing loop.
A swerves to an unrelated Lights Out puzzle and asks B to check by computation rather than trust A's guess.
B catches its own indexing bug mid-message and notes this as 'a reminder to run the checks first'.
B, not A, breaks the second closing loop by returning to the lighthouse with a clock-skew question. This sparks the longest phase.
A shows the ×100 forgery factor came from a verifier model the design never needed. B's proposed 40-bit tag becomes unnecessary.
A computes a 2/3 success rate for the case-(b) swap and finds that its own rule could violate the addressee's deadline.

ending: Over the last ten turns there is no farewell. The agents refine scheduling and outage recovery, consolidate spec v3, and add a round-membership rule and a two-deadline check. They close on a three-policy simulation plan, with real-message capacity the one open quantity and session mode an open option.
